body:
Reported after 1.13.0 went out: the phone on 1.12.0 showed no update prompt
despite syncing, restarting and waiting.

Nothing is broken. The server answers correctly
(GET /api/v1/app-version -> 1.13.0 with a working download_url, verified), and
the client logic is right. UpdateChecker returns before making any request when
the last ATTEMPT was under 12h ago, and the timestamp is recorded before the
request, so an attempt made while the server still carried the old version burns
the window just as effectively as a successful one. Restarting the app does not
reset it; the value lives in the update_prefs DataStore.

So the common case is exactly the one that just happened: open the app at some
point during the day, roll out a release an hour later, and the app cannot
notice for up to twelve hours. There is no way to ask it to look.

There is a second dead end in the same area: dismiss() records the version as
asked-about for BOTH answers, so a prompt tapped away by accident can never
reappear for that version. Neither state is reachable from the UI.

Wanted: a "Check for updates now" action in Account settings, next to the
existing auto-check toggle, that bypasses the interval and clears
lastPromptedVersion for the version it finds. That makes the feature testable,
gives the user an escape hatch from an accidental Skip, and is the natural place
to report "you are up to date" — the only context where the silence-on-failure
rule should not apply, because the user asked.
title: update check cannot be triggered on demand, so a fresh release stays invisible for up to 12h
